authorities.compatibilityNote: The backend emits the explicit capability set and enforces it on protected routes. Portal and Mobile consume that set before any role-based fallback; the remaining role tables are limited to sessions issued before the capability contract. Admin Global consumes the separate Platform capability response owned by backend Platform RBAC.

authorities.prePhysicalImpact: The transition is intentional and non-blocking for device testing: backend journey transitions remain authoritative, legacy mutations are tenant-bound and concurrency-checked, and offline actions reconcile through the same backend session authority.
authorities.closureCondition: All Mobile and Portal consumers use the journey transition contract, production contains no unreconciled legacy route sessions, and the legacy navigation mutation endpoints can be removed with their compatibility tests.

authorities.remainingWork: Replace route-specific error payloads and client-specific parsing with one versioned API error contract carrying stable code, safe message, traceId, retry/recoverability metadata and HTTP status semantics. Portal, Mobile and Admin Global must then consume that shared envelope instead of maintaining product-specific classifiers.
authorities.prePhysicalImpact: The partial contract is non-blocking for the pre-physical build because central containment and trace IDs are active, critical authentication/session and rate-limit failures have explicit tested policies, and Admin Global now preserves HTTP status, code and retryability instead of collapsing transient and authoritative failures into Error(message). Remaining divergence affects cross-product diagnostic consistency rather than authorization or data ownership.
authorities.closureCondition: All backend routes emit the shared error envelope and Mobile, Portal and Admin Global consume its code, traceId and recoverability fields without ad hoc status/message reinterpretation.

knownDivergences.summary: The dependency graph contains iOS tooling, but the repository has no mobile/ios native project and CI does not certify an iOS artifact; iOS is not a current release target.
Backend tests are maintained as one long shell chain instead of stable domain suites.
mobile/app.json is the compiled runtime version authority while mobile/package.json retains independent package metadata and must not be treated as the release version.
The active mobile appearance authority is account-scoped, but root-store still retains the old device-global THEME_KEY/setThemeMode path as dead compatibility residue.
Release-candidate and historical reports remain distributed across the repository root and docs without a canonical archive policy.

Admin Global code is integrated; DNS and both Cloudflare Access perimeters are externally reachable, Render rejects Platform traffic without Access, and CORS accepts the private Admin origin. Real Platform authentication, the production platform_owner, MFA lifecycle and authenticated production certification remain external P0 release gates that repository CI and unauthenticated probes cannot prove.
